maya: Heads up — CI linkcheck failed on a bunch of cross-page links after the docs PR (rendering changes). It looks like links to headings that include inline code stop resolving. kevin: Example of the failure? can you paste the linkcheck output? maya: Sure: ``` WARN: docs/getting-started.md: broken fragment: ./guides/redis.md#configure--redis WARN: docs/guides/redis.md: fragment not found: #configure--redis ``` The target heading is `## Configure `--redis` (with backticks), so the slug the site generates doesn't match the link. alicia: yup — we recently flipped the slugifier to preserve punctuation in some cases; MkDocs vs Docusaurus handle backticks differently. That change surfaced now. kevin: Minimal fix options: 1) change the link target to the generated slug, 2) add an explicit header id, or 3) normalize slug generator in the build. I'd prefer (2) for a targeted, low-risk change. maya: Adding an explicit id is fine for MkDocs: `## Configure `--redis` {#configure-redis}`. For Docusaurus we need to use `

Configure --redis

` or add frontmatter `slug`? Ugh. sam: I'll open a quick PR to add explicit ids on the 4 affected pages and update the problematic links. I'll include a note and a small test for linkcheck in CI to run against the new slug behaviour. ETA EOD :white_check_mark: docs-bot: linkcheck-job: re-run scheduled for PR #4521 kevin: Great — once PR is up I'll review. if we see many occurrences we can look at reverting the slugifier change. maya: Thanks everyone — will peek at the PR and help validate once deployed to staging :tada:
